item.title: Higher Ed News Digest — Monday, 10 August 2026
item.description:
Coverage window: Friday 7 August – Monday 10 August 2026. Sixteen stories, read by two voices.

In this episode

  1. Heritage Foundation publishes model state legislation to codify the federal compact
  2. Who drafted "Compact 2.0" — and what presidents are being told to do about it
  3. Professors are retiring early, and AI is the deciding factor
  4. Four clocks on campus AI, and Turnitin's move to keystroke monitoring
  5. Fisk's $400 million data center becomes a flashpoint
  6. Civil rights enforcement widens, with Duke Law a first
  7. Federal policy roundup: an OPT fee, a Senate package, a grant-rule block, and a scholarship portal
  8. Workforce Pell: the policy is live, the states are not ready
  9. Texas: the performance funding model worked too well to afford
  10. State aid shortfalls are common, and the design invites them
  11. Howard offers buyouts to 600 employees
  12. Illinois Tech and Mankato cut deep, days before term
  13. GAO: 94% of Division I athletics programs lost money
  14. Price competition at both ends: Boston University and Alaska
  15. Niche: 61% of colleges met fall goals, but only half of small ones
  16. Digital learning: cheaper materials, LMS fragility, and new autumn programmes

One thing to watch: tying money to outcomes is easy to legislate and expensive to honour — the compact fight moves to fifty state capitals just as Texas discovers it cannot afford the performance model everyone praised.

Sources

The compact and federal policy

  • Codify the Federal Higher Education Compact — Heritage Foundation
  • The Heritage Foundation releases sweeping model bill to overhaul higher ed — Higher Ed Dive
  • College Leaders Play Down Their Involvement in 'Compact 2.0' — The Chronicle of Higher Education
  • Here's the Latest News on Trump and Higher Ed — The Chronicle of Higher Education (WashU faculty-led process, Yale billboards, CareerOneStop, Senate grant-rule block, Duke Law findings)
  • How Should Leaders Respond to McMahon's Letter? — Inside Higher Ed
  • Linda McMahon's Trojan Horse (opinion) — Inside Higher Ed
  • Committee OKs bill to block Education Department transfers — Higher Ed Dive
  • Week in review: A $100K fee for OPT? — Higher Ed Dive
  • 2026 Gainful Employment — NASFAA
  • Department of Education finalizes OBBB higher ed accountability rule — Nixon Peabody

State policy and student aid

  • Texas Could Shortchange New Funding Model Champions — Inside Higher Ed
  • State Aid Shortfalls Are Common. Can They Be Addressed? — Inside Higher Ed
  • States Wrestle With Data and Program Tweaks to Access Workforce Pell — Inside Higher Ed

AI and academic integrity

  • These Professors Are Retiring Early. AI Was the Last Straw. — The Chronicle of Higher Education
  • My Students Weren't Human. They Were Ghosts. — The Chronicle Review
  • AI Is a Wicked Problem. That's the University's Specialty. — The Chronicle Review
  • To Catch AI Cheating, Turnitin Wants to Monitor Students' Keystrokes — The Chronicle of Higher Education
  • Will a Data Center Bring Risk or Reward to Fisk? — Inside Higher Ed

Legal and civil rights

  • Justice Department finds Duke Law School discriminates based on race in admissions — U.S. Department of Justice
  • ED investigates alleged antisemitic harassment at two California universities — U.S. Department of Education
  • Haverford Settles Antisemitism Lawsuit — Inside Higher Ed
  • The professor, Israel, Gaza and the University of Minnesota — The Guardian

Institutional finance

  • Here's the Latest News on Campus Finance — The Chronicle of Higher Education (GAO athletics figures, Illinois Tech, Mankato, Alaska)
  • Howard U. Offers Buyouts to 600 Employees — The Chronicle of Higher Education
  • Illinois Institute of Technology lays off 160 faculty and staff members — Higher Ed Dive
  • Minnesota State Mankato to undergo layoffs, hike tuition amid $22M shortfall — Higher Ed Dive
  • BU Offers Free Tuition to Families Earning Up to $200K — Inside Higher Ed
  • U. of Alaska Plans to End Out-of-State Tuition Rates — Inside Higher Ed

Enrolment and admissions

  • 61 Percent of Colleges Have Met Their Enrollment Goals for Fall 2026 — Inside Higher Ed (Niche survey)
  • The 'Fraud Squad' at Caltech Will Catch You if You Lie on Your Application — The Wall Street Journal
  • 'Why Yale' prompt exploring identity axed from first-year application — Yale Daily News
  • Why You Don't Even Have to Apply for College Anymore — Bloomberg
  • Open Doors international student enrollment trends — Institute of International Education

Online and digital learning

  • Digital Boom Drives Down Cost of College Course Materials — Inside Higher Ed (NACS Student Watch)
  • When the LMS Goes Dark: Rethinking Contingency Planning in Higher Ed — WCET Frontiers
  • Writing the Next Chapter: Distance Learning in the American Higher Ed Story — WCET Frontiers
  • Studios — Virtual Environments Studio — Virginia Tech University Libraries
  • Northwest Nazarene University to launch four accelerated online degrees — Idaho News
  • University launches 2 new online master's programs for fall 2026 — University of Miami

Higher Ed News Digest is compiled twice weekly, on Mondays and Thursdays.
